description: Search, filter, sort, or retrieve by ID. Covers all OpenAlex entity types (works, authors, sources, institutions, topics, keywords, publishers, funders, awards). Pass `id` to retrieve a single entity. Otherwise, use `query` and/or `filters` for discovery. Filters take a record object; an unambiguous native string such as "issn:0920-8542" is also accepted when enabled and disclosed in `notice`. Native clauses split on commas outside paired double quotes and the first colon; duplicate keys and bare fragments are rejected. Any filter value sent unquoted must have paired double quotes; balanced search phrases remain valid. Supports keyword search with boolean operators, exact phrase matching, AI semantic search, and seeded random samples. Use openalex_resolve_name to resolve names to IDs before filtering. Searches and ID lookups return a curated set of fields by default; pass `select` to override with specific fields, or `["*"]` for the full record. A page holds `per_page` records and `next_cursor` continues it — semantic search and a seeded `sample` continue with `page` instead; an `id` lookup returns every selected array whole, and `slice` pages one array by count.

cursor.description: Pagination cursor from a previous response. Pass to get the next page. Omit it on the first call — an empty string is rejected, since a supplied-but-blank cursor is a caller mistake rather than a request for page 1. Keyword and exact modes only — semantic search walks its candidates with `page`, and a `cursor` sent with it is rejected.

entity_type.description: Type of scholarly entity to search.

filters.description: Filter criteria as field:value pairs. AND across fields (multiple keys). OR within field: pipe-separate ("us|gb"). NOT: prefix "!" ("!us"). Range: "2020-2024". Comparison: ">100", "<50". AND within same field: "+"-separate ("us+gb"); inside a `.search` value, a DOI, a date (a timestamp's "+00:00" offset), a URL field such as landing_page_url, an exactly matched name (display_name, awards.funder_display_name — "C++", "Erasmus+"), a biblio field (issue "1+2"), or awards.funder_award_id, "+" is a literal character. A value cannot mix "|" with an AND operator — a "+", or a space between values on an ID, code, or `language` key (a space inside a language name is part of the name, and a country field never reads a space as AND) — OpenAlex splits it on "|" first and drops every alternative that ANDs more than one value, so such a value is rejected; put the AND in a second key instead ("institutions.country_code": "US" beside "authorships.institutions.country_code": "DE|FR" on works). On a field matched as whole text (display_name, awards.funder_display_name, awards.funder_award_id, geo.city, geo.region, raw_affiliation_strings, block_key, biblio fields), a space is part of the value: "New York", "!New York", and "New York|Boston" match as written, but quotes around one "|" alternative make that alternative match nothing. A comma is part of such a value too ("University of California, Berkeley" on raw_affiliation_strings): a value holding one is sent as one quoted phrase, its "+" a literal character. A value sent as a quoted phrase cannot contain a double quote of its own. A multi-word value there cannot be ANDed with another ("New York+Boston" matches nothing); to require two funders or institutions, AND their IDs (awards.funder_id, authorships.institutions.id). Country fields (keys ending in country_code, country_codes, or countries) take ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes ("DE"): an alpha-3 code ("DEU"), numeric code ("276"), or English name ("Germany", "South Korea") is converted, "UK" becomes "GB", and a value that cannot be a country code is rejected. A space there is part of a name, never a separator: "South Korea|Japan" ORs two countries, and "DE US" is rejected. `language` takes ISO 639-1 codes ("en"): an ISO 639-2 code ("eng") or English name ("English") is converted. Two keys that resolve to the same upstream field (an alias and its canonical name, e.g. `year` and `publication_year`) are both applied and AND'd, so they narrow rather than override each other. Use OpenAlex IDs (not names) for entity filters — resolve names first. Common keys: `openalex` (filter by entity ID, e.g. {"openalex": "W123|W456"}), `cites` (works citing a given work), `publication_year` (range "2020-2024"), `authorships.author.id`, `type`, `is_oa`.

id.description: Retrieve a single entity by ID. Supports: OpenAlex ID ("W2741809807", or its OpenAlex record-page or API URL such as "https://openalex.org/works/W2741809807" or "https://api.openalex.org/works/W2741809807"), whose letter must name `entity_type` — W works, A authors, S sources, I institutions, T topics, P publishers, F funders, G awards; DOI ("10.1038/nature12373"; under entity_type "funders", a funder's Crossref Funder Registry DOI such as "10.13039/100000001"), ORCID ("0000-0002-1825-0097"), ROR ("https://ror.org/00hx57361" — one ROR can name an institution, a funder, and a publisher, and `entity_type` picks which), PMID ("12345678" or "https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/12345678"), ISSN ("1234-5678"). Keywords are identified by slug rather than a native ID — pass either the slug ("groundwater") or the URL a search returns ("https://openalex.org/keywords/groundwater"). A PMCID is recognized too, bare ("PMC1234567") or as a PubMed Central URL, but OpenAlex indexes no PMCIDs, so it resolves nothing — pass the work's PMID or DOI instead. When provided, `query`, `search_mode`, `filters`, `sort`, `sample`, and `seed` are not applied — the returned record is the entity at that ID regardless of them, and the response `notice` names any you passed. `select` still applies: the curated per-entity-type default is returned unless you pass `select` (use `["*"]` for the complete record). Every selected array returns whole; `slice` pages a long one by count. To filter, drop `id` and search. Use openalex_resolve_name to find the ID if unknown.

page.description: Page number (1-based) for semantic search and for a seeded `sample`, the two searches that paginate with `page` instead of `cursor`. Semantic search ranks a query-dependent candidate set whose size `meta.count` reports, so the last reachable page is ceil(meta.count / per_page) — e.g. page 14 for a count of 70 with per_page=5. A sample draws min(sample, meta.count) records, so its last page is ceil(min(sample, meta.count) / per_page); paging a sample requires `seed`, and OpenAlex serves only its first 10,000 records, so a page × per_page above 10,000 is rejected. Passing it with any other search is rejected.

per_page.description: Results per page. Default 25, or under `sample` the sample size up to 100, so a sample of 100 or fewer returns whole in one call. A larger value returns at most 100 and says so — at most 50 under search_mode "semantic", which OpenAlex also limits to about 1 request per second. A server set to OPENALEX_CLAMP_PER_PAGE=false rejects a value over either cap instead. An `id` lookup ignores page size.

query.description: Text search query. Supports boolean operators (AND, OR, NOT), quoted phrases ("exact match"), wildcards (machin*), fuzzy matching (machin~1), and proximity ("climate change"~5). Omit for filter-only queries — an empty string is rejected, since a blank search is a mistake rather than a request for the whole catalog.

sample.description: Return a random sample of this many entities matching the filters, up to 10,000; a larger value draws 10,000 and says so (rejected instead on a server set to OPENALEX_CLAMP_PER_PAGE=false). The sample comes back `per_page` records at a time — by default the whole sample up to 100 — and a larger one is walked with `page` and a `seed`, which fixes the draw; without `seed` only its first page is returned. `meta.count` stays the population matching the filters. Keyword and exact modes only: OpenAlex does not sample a semantic search, so `sample` with search_mode "semantic" is rejected. Cannot be combined with `cursor` or `sort` — a sample has no order, and a search passing either is rejected. Useful for unbiased exploration: spot-checking filter correctness, stratified review prompts, or generating exploration sets without bias toward most-cited.

search_mode.description: Search strategy. "keyword": stemmed full-text (default). "exact": no stemming, matches individual words (use quoted phrases for multi-word exact match). "semantic": AI embedding similarity over a query-dependent candidate set whose size `meta.count` reports, at ~1 req/sec, up to 50 per page, and paginated with `page` rather than `cursor`.

seed.description: Deterministic seed for `sample`. Same seed + same filters = the same draw, page for page — required to walk a sample larger than one page with `page`, and worth passing whenever reproducibility matters. Has no effect without `sample`, and a search that passes it alone is rejected.

select.description: OpenAlex top-level field names to return. Always returned: `id`, `display_name` — additional fields you list are appended. A curated default per entity type applies to both searches and single-entity (`id`) lookups; pass field names to override it, or `["*"]` to retrieve the complete record (every field). Only top-level fields project, so a nested value is requested by its parent object: bibliometrics (`h_index`, `i10_index`, `2yr_mean_citedness`) live under `summary_stats` on authors, sources, institutions, publishers, and funders, and naming a leaf returns that object. On sources, `publisher` returns `host_organization_name`: the publisher of a journal, the hosting institution of a repository, and null on most sources. On works, `author_list` returns each author in authorship order as `{id, display_name, orcid}` (`orcid` null when absent), a compact alternative to `authorships`, which also carries institutions and affiliations; neither the default nor `["*"]` includes it. Invalid field names produce an error identifying the rejected field. A wide projection on a large page makes a large response, so name the fields you need. Not applied with `slice`. Example: ["doi", "author_list", "primary_topic"].

slice.description: Page one array of the record at `id`: returns `id`, `display_name`, and `limit` elements of `field` from `offset` — fewer only at the array end — with the window in `windows`, whose `next` call repeats `limit` from the following offset. Requires `id`; replaces `select`. An offset at or past the end returns an empty window. A 100-author list cap can be continued on the singleton; at 5,000 stored authors the byline remains possibly capped, but `next` is null once stored entries are exhausted.

field.description: Top-level array field to page, such as "authorships", "author_list", or "referenced_works". Leave it empty to skip slicing.

limit.description: Elements to return. Default 50; a larger value returns at most 5,000 and says so (rejected instead on a server set to OPENALEX_CLAMP_PER_PAGE=false).

offset.description: 0-based index of the first element to return.

sort.description: Sort field. Prefix with "-" for descending. Comma-separate for a multi-key sort, applied left to right, with the "-" prefix set per key ("-publication_year,cited_by_count" sorts by year descending, then citations ascending). Common: "cited_by_count", "-publication_date", "-relevance_score" (default when query present). Note: when combined with a keyword query, an explicit sort overrides relevance ranking entirely — top results may be highly cited but only tangentially on-topic. Use "-relevance_score" or omit sort to keep the most relevant results first. "-relevance_score" requires an active search via "query" or a "filter:search" filter — passing it without one will fail. Not combinable with `sample` — a search passing both is rejected.

name: openalex_search_entities

budget.description: What this call cost against the OpenAlex daily budget and what is left of it. Price a full traversal before committing to it: `totalCount` ÷ `per_page` × `costUsd` against `remainingUsd`. Absent when OpenAlex omitted the accounting headers.

costUsd.description: USD this call spent. 0 for an `id` lookup by an OpenAlex ID, DOI, ORCID, ROR, PMID, or ISSN — OpenAlex does not bill those single-entity fetches, so batching known IDs beats paging a filtered list. OpenAlex bills like one list request a keyword looked up by its slug, an `id` carrying characters past the identifier itself (`W2741809807#x` still returns W2741809807), and a funder looked up by its Funder Registry DOI.

prepaidRemainingUsd.description: USD left in the prepaid balance — a separate pool OpenAlex draws on only after the daily allowance runs out, and which the daily reset does not refill. Add it to `remainingUsd` for the full spendable amount. Absent when the account holds no prepaid balance.

remainingUsd.description: USD left in today's OpenAlex budget after this call.

resetsInSeconds.description: Seconds until the daily budget refills (midnight UTC).

echo.description: Compact echo of the criteria that actually ran (entity_type, query, filters, sort, search_mode) — surfaces what was searched when results are empty. An `id` lookup echoes entity_type and id alone, because the search criteria are not applied on that path.

error.description: Present when the call failed. Absent on success.

code.description: JSON-RPC error code for this failure.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure mode. Declared by this tool: `invalid_filter_string`: A native filter string has an incomplete clause or unmatched double quotes. `duplicate_filter_string_key`: A native filter string repeats an exact key. `unmatched_quote_in_filter_value`: A filter value sent unquoted has an unmatched double quote. `semantic_per_page_cap`: A semantic search (no `id`) set per_page above its cap of 50 on a server with OPENALEX_CLAMP_PER_PAGE=false; with clamping on (the default), it returns 50 and says so. `response_too_large`: The response's structuredContent or content[] text would exceed 8,000,000 bytes — a wide `select` on a large page, or a record with very long arrays. A page is never shortened to fit. `semantic_without_query`: A search set search_mode to "semantic" without supplying the `query` it embeds. `semantic_with_cursor`: A search set search_mode to "semantic" and supplied `cursor`, which OpenAlex rejects on a semantic query. `page_without_semantic`: A search supplied `page` with neither search_mode "semantic" nor `sample`. `sample_with_cursor`: A search (no `id`) provided both `sample` and `cursor`. `sample_page_without_seed`: A search (no `id`) provided `page` with `sample` but no `seed`, which OpenAlex refuses: an unseeded sample redraws on every call, so its pages would overlap. `sample_page_too_deep`: A sample page reaches past record 10,000 (`page` × `per_page` above 10,000), the most of a sample OpenAlex serves by page number. `sample_with_semantic`: A search (no `id`) provided `sample` with search_mode "semantic", which OpenAlex does not sample — it returns the same ranked candidates under every seed. `sample_with_sort`: A search (no `id`) provided both `sample` and `sort`, which OpenAlex refuses together. `seed_without_sample`: A search (no `id`) provided `seed` without `sample`. `slice_without_id`: A search passed `slice` without `id` — slice pages one array of one record. `slice_field_not_array`: The `slice` field is `*`, or is not an array on the record at `id` — absent, null, a scalar, or an object. `id_type_mismatch`: `id` is a native OpenAlex ID whose letter names another entity type than `entity_type`, or a concept ID (C…), a type this server does not serve. `id_dot_segment`: `id` holds a `.` or `..` path segment, written plainly or percent-encoded. `entity_not_found`: Lookup by id matched no OpenAlex entity. `rate_limited`: OpenAlex throttled the request for exceeding its per-second ceiling (HTTP 429). `upstream_budget_exhausted`: The OpenAlex daily usage budget is spent (HTTP 429). `upstream_plan_required`: A filter is one OpenAlex serves only on a paid plan — created_date, updated_date, or a from_/to_ form of either (HTTP 429 "Plan upgrade required"). `upstream_timeout`: OpenAlex did not respond within the request deadline. `upstream_unavailable`: OpenAlex was unreachable or unusable — HTTP 503, a connection failure, a body that was empty, HTML, or unparseable JSON, or a semantic search whose query embedding failed upstream (HTTP 400 `Failed to embed query:`, or semantic search not configured). `upstream_unauthorized`: OpenAlex rejected the API key (HTTP 401). `upstream_forbidden`: OpenAlex denied access to the requested resource (HTTP 403). `comma_in_filter_value`: A filter value contains a comma, which collides with the OpenAlex filter separator, on a field that takes no phrase. Free-text search filters (any `.search` key, such as title.search or abstract.search.exact) and fields matched as whole text (display_name, awards.funder_display_name, awards.funder_award_id, geo.city, geo.region, raw_affiliation_strings, block_key, parsed_longest_name, biblio fields) are exempt: a comma there is sent quoted, as part of the phrase. `invalid_country_code`: A country filter (a key ending in country_code, country_codes, or countries) holds a segment that cannot be a country code, such as a misspelled name, an unassigned number, "unknown", or two codes joined by a space ("DE US"). `mixed_and_or_in_filter_value`: A filter value puts "|" (OR) beside an AND operator — a "+", or a space on a field where words mean AND (on a country field a space is always part of a country name, and inside a language name it is part of the name). OpenAlex splits the value on "|" first and drops every alternative that ANDs more than one value, so no single value can carry both. `quote_in_filter_value`: A filter value sent to OpenAlex double-quoted holds a double quote inside its outer pair — a value the server quotes (a multi-word value on a field matched as whole text, or a value holding a comma on such a field or on a free-text search filter), or one the caller wrapped in double quotes on any filter but a free-text search. `upstream_invalid_params`: OpenAlex rejected an invalid filter, select, or sort field name (HTTP 400). `upstream_invalid_id_value`: An entity-ID filter received a value that is not an OpenAlex ID — usually a name (HTTP 400). `upstream_sort_requires_search`: sort=-relevance_score was used without an active search (HTTP 400). `query_too_long`: OpenAlex rejected `query` as longer than the search length it accepts (HTTP 400). `upstream_invalid_params_other`: OpenAlex rejected the request (HTTP 400) for a reason other than an invalid field name. `upstream_validation_failed`: OpenAlex rejected the request as semantically invalid (HTTP 422). Other values are possible when a failure originates below the handler.

recovery.description: Actionable next step for the caller.

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

count.description: Total results matching the query/filters — under `sample` too, whose draw holds min(sample, count) records. Under search_mode "semantic" it is instead the size of the ranked candidate set — the most results `page` can reach — not an exhaustive match total.

next_cursor.description: Cursor for the next page; pass it back unchanged as `cursor`. null when no further page exists — always under semantic search and `sample`, which continue with `page` — except on a final page that exactly fills `per_page`: OpenAlex still returns a cursor there, and it leads to an empty page.

per_page.description: Page size OpenAlex echoed for this request — the applied per_page after clamping or its default, not the number of records returned. A singleton reports 1. A short or exhausted page carries fewer records than this.

notice.description: Guidance notice. Set when per_page, sample, or slice.limit was clamped (requested and applied sizes), a native filter string was converted, a first call has no matches, a continuation is exhausted, an id lookup ignores search criteria, semantic search reports a candidate total and whether a later `page` holds more, a sample draws more than one page (the next `page`, its last page, or that `seed` makes it pageable), an author array is possibly capped (100 list entries or 5,000 stored singleton entries), a slice offset is past the end, or slice replaces select. Absent otherwise.

results.description: OpenAlex entity objects. Text values are plain text — HTML entities decoded, HTML/JATS/MathML markup removed — except identifier and URL fields such as `id`, `doi`, `ids`, and `*_url`, returned exactly as OpenAlex stores them; an abstract arrives reconstructed as `abstract`, and a selected `author_list` as one `{id, display_name, orcid}` entry per author. Additional fields depend on entity_type and select. Possibly capped author arrays and `slice` windows are in `windows`.

items.description: A single OpenAlex entity record. `id` is always present and `display_name` is always returned (though it may be null); additional fields vary by entity_type and `select`.

display_name.description: Entity name or work title. null when OpenAlex holds no title for the record (paratext works and other untitled entries) — use `id` to identify it.

id.description: OpenAlex ID URL (e.g., "https://openalex.org/W2741809807"). `windows` names records by the bare ID ("W2741809807"); a keyword keeps its URL.

totalCount.description: Total results matching the query/filters across all pages.

windows.description: Author arrays possibly capped at 100 on a list record or 5,000 stored on a singleton, and the window of every `slice` call — present even when the slice holds the whole array. A slice window's `next` repeats its `slice.limit` from the following offset; `next` is null at the stored-array end, including a possibly capped singleton.

items.description: An array returned in part, or possibly in part.

next.description: `id` + `slice` call for the next elements; null at the array end.

offset.description: Index of the first element shown.

possibly_capped.description: True for exactly 100 authorships or author_list entries on a list record, or 5,000 on a singleton lookup: the byline may be longer than the returned array.

total.description: Stored array length returned to this call, not a complete byline total.

title: Openalex Search Entities
